newsitem.title: USA: Black U.S. lawmakers say army sex probe contaminated.
newsitem.headline: Black U.S. lawmakers say army sex probe contaminated.

text.p: Leading black members of Congress visited the Army's Aberdeen Proving Ground on Monday and said an investigation into sexual misconduct at the base was "contaminated" by credible charges of coercion.
The lawmakers also said the probe should not be allowed to continue without an outside investigation.

"Having come here today we are more convinced than ever that something is amiss, something is wrong," Representative Maxine Waters, a California Democrat and head of the Congressional Black Caucus, told a news conference after the visit.
"We certainly heard from drill sergeants and recruits about coercion. This theme ran throughout all conversations we had today," she said.
Asked whether the army's probe should go on, or await an independent investigation, Waters said, "I don't think it makes good sense to let a contaminated investigation continue."
Waters led a five-member caucus delegation to the base on Monday where they met with about 20 sergeants and 20 recruits.

The handling of a sexual misconduct investigation that began last year erupted as an issue last week when five white women said they had been pressured by army investigators to accuse higher ranking soldiers, who were black, of rape.
The women said they resisted the pressure and they believed any relationships they had had with the accused men did not amount to rape.

The eight black soldiers at the base have been charged with rape or other sexual violations in connection with the probe. One of those charged had been involved with one of the women who came forward last week, but his charges were not related to that involvement.

The National Association for Advancement of Coloured People, saying it was concerned about the possibility of civil rights violations, called for an independent investigation of the Army's probe of sexual misconduct at Aberdeen.
Army Secretary Togo West has rejected the call for an independent investigation.
The Black Caucus members said drill instructors they met with on Monday did not say they viewed race as a factor in the probe, but did not rule it out.
Representative Elijah Cummings, a Democrat from Maryland, said morale had suffered on the base as a result of the probe.
Waters said she was concerned because there was a history of black men in the United States being targeted with rape accusations from white women.
Aberdeen base officials declined to comment on the congressional delegation's visit.
